newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Arab fund earmarks $500 mln for private sector.
newsitem.headline: Arab fund earmarks $500 mln for private sector.

text.p: The Arab world's leading soft-loan agency has approved a $500 million programme to help boost private sector development in Arab countries, a Gulf Arab minister said.
"It has been approved. This is a new window that will be created within the framework of the fund," Bahraini Finance and National Economy Minister Ibrahim Abdel-Karim told Reuters.
The decision was taken during an annual meeting of Arab finance ministers and central bank governors, who on Sunday began their second day of talks in Abu Dhabi.

The programme is part of the Kuwait-based Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development, owned by 20 Arab governments and the Palestine Liberation Organisation. The fund lends at interest rates of three to five percent over 20 to 25 years mainly to projects that promote Arab economic coordination.
Infrastructure projects such as power, communications and water take priority.

"Now as the private sector is taking a much bigger role in the development of Arab economies, it is time that we allocate part of the resources in this fund to invest in the private sector," Abdel-Karim said.

Under the terms of the programme, private sector companies or investors will be able to borrow directly from the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development and not have to secure guarantees from its member governments, he added.
